title: Mexican embassy, Washington, to the consul at Eagle Pass, 17 Apr 1917: a reciprocal one-alphabet telegram sent as "clave Murciélago", read in part

documents.shelfmark: AHGE-SRE, Archivo de la Embajada de México en Estados Unidos, leg. 507, exp. 6 (not seen); text from Narváez 2019, p. 339, fig. 10

plaintext.source: Typed repetition of a telegram of 16 April; heading and address in clear; no contemporary decipherment known. Narváez prints no reading.

transcription.source: photographs of the halftone figure in Narváez 2019, p. 339, fig. 10 (loan copy); archive image not seen

system.summary: Simple substitution with a reciprocal alphabet made from the keyword TIRANO: TIRANOBCDEFGHJKLMPQSUVWXYZ folded on itself, giving A-X, B-U, C-S, D-Q, E-P, F-M, G-L, H-K, I-Z, N-W, O-V, R-Y, with T and J standing for themselves (H, J, K unseen in the text); irregular group lengths, word division lost. Not the Murciélago square named in the heading.
system.sibling_key: The 1915 'Clave Garduño' table printed by Narváez (2019, p. 311) is the same construction with the keyword GARDUÑO on 27 letters; not this key. Found by our construction search, not used in the solve.

prior_solution.where: Narváez 2019 (pp. 338-342) pictures the telegram and says it stayed impenetrable to the consul; he prints no reading. Not in the repository (catalogue, leads, known.py, 23 Nov 2026) or in Narváez's 2025 Historia Mexicana article; web searches for its phrases found nothing.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling photographed the Narváez book, chose the target and set the rules (frozen plan, blind transcriptions, controls, independent review); AI agents transcribed, solved, reviewed and wrote up. No person has checked the reading.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Andrew Beling

solution.what: Two transcriptions from the book photographs, the second blind; a third, blind, by an independent reviewer. 246 letters each; they differ only at the doubtful letters listed in NOTES.
The book's Murciélago square with key word 31 of the printed consular list (Escultor), plan frozen first.
Index of coincidence 0.071, flat over periods 1-12: one alphabet, not a repeating key.

Plan hashed before the runs; the solver on three shuffles of the 246 letters (best -2924 to -2964, no Spanish) and on three 246-letter passages of real Spanish under random keys (99.2-99.6% of letters right).

Simple substitution solve on Spanish letter 4-grams, 40 restarts per text; the rare letters D, L, M, N, O set by the reciprocal pairing and the sense. Held-out: the key from letters 1-170 reads 171-246 unchanged apart from the slips and cipher K (absent from 1-170).

Keyword-mixed alphabets set against the plain alphabet (3,791 keywords incl. MURCIELAGO, both directions, 26 offsets): best score -3144.2, below the shuffles; not a shifted keyword alphabet. Folding was not tried in this step (see the key-construction step).

Independent reviewer (an AI agent of ours, Claude Opus 5.5, 23 Nov 2026 00:20-00:45 EST): own blind transcription, own solver and corpus (Spanish Wikipedia), before seeing this work: same key, same sentence word for word.

Key construction: TIRANO was noticed by eye in the recovered pairs before the plan was written; then checked under a frozen plan: the pairs are the keyword alphabet TIRANO + rest folded on itself; about 23,000 keywords, 26/27-letter alphabets, folds and two-row pairings (3.7 million keys); TIRANO is the only fit. The telegram fixes 11 pairs and T (12 facts); chance fit about 1 in 10 million over the search; positive control (50/50) is a code check, random control 0/3,000. Predicts H = k, K = h, J = j (letters that never occur).

Telegraphic Spanish read end to end: 26 of 37 words clean; 11 words with holes: nine shown to be sender's slips (five are e/t exchanges), one probable slip (241, F/P) and one overtyped letter (40), all read from the sense.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 246 tokens, 21 types, es-modern order 4: reading -2.752 per letter; random keys -7.254 (z 6.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.784 (mean -4.018, z 9.1); annealer on the real text -3.234. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.054; polyphony 0.053; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.234

outcome.method_basis: Simulated annealing on Spanish letter statistics, validated by shuffled and enciphered controls at this length and by an independent blind solve; the rare letters fixed by the reciprocal pairing the other 18 letters show.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 26/37 words come out of the key uncorrected with the readings in transcription.txt (159/246 letters); 25/37 if position 121 is N; 11 holes, every one completed from the sense.

gaps.detail: whether the sender corrected the letter can only be seen on the archive original (AHGE-SRE, AEMEUA leg. 507, exp. 6)

gaps.item: positions 121, 129, 241 and the other doubtful letters
gaps.detail: F/P, M/N, W/F at the limit of the book's halftone; with every preferred reading of the fourth blind reading 23 of 37 words are clean

gaps.item: nine sender's slips read from the sense
gaps.detail: clear in all four readings of the photograph; only the original can confirm them
the second key list is in the same file and not printed

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #944 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Read decryption.txt against reading.md: telegraphic Spanish running end to end; 26 of 37 words come out of the key uncorrected, 11 carry a one-letter slip read from the sense (listed by position). Key rebuilt from the TIRANO fold rule equals key.tsv; decryption reproduced group for group. Short-text floor: 11 holes, read in part.

texts.summary: Asks the consul, for the censorship committee appointed by President Wilson (which fits the Committee on Public Information, created 13 April 1917), for the names of journalists and information agents spreading false news, chiefly of German plots, with proof if needed.
